findings.title: NPE potential when all-groups resource lookup returns null
findings.body: In GroupPermissionsV2.hasPermission, when the per-group lookup fails the code calls `resource = AdminPermissionsSchema.SCHEMA.getResourceTypeResource(session, server, AdminPermissionsSchema.GROUPS_RESOURCE_TYPE);` and on the next line dereferences it directly with `if (policyStore.findByResource(server, resource).isEmpty())`. getResourceTypeResource can return null when supportsAuthorizationSchema is false or when the synthetic all-groups resource has not been created. The missing null check will throw NullPointerException on the first FGAP V2 group-evaluation call that hits this path. The guard must be `resource == null || policyStore.findByResource(server, resource).isEmpty()` (or equivalent) before evaluating permissions.

findings.title: Same NPE pattern in UserPermissionsV2.hasPermission fallback
findings.body: UserPermissionsV2.hasPermission assigns `resource = AdminPermissionsSchema.SCHEMA.getResourceTypeResource(session, server, AdminPermissionsSchema.USERS_RESOURCE_TYPE);` and immediately dereferences it on the next line in `policyStore.findByResource(server, resource).isEmpty()`. If the all-users resource does not exist (e.g., schema not yet initialised) this throws NullPointerException, breaking V2 per-user evaluations (canView/canManage/canMapRoles/canImpersonate/canManageGroupMembership on a specific user). A null guard before the policy lookup is required.

findings.title: getGroupIdsWithViewPermission only sees the all-groups resource, ignoring individual group permissions
findings.body: The implementation iterates `resourceStore.findByType(server, AdminPermissionsSchema.GROUPS_RESOURCE_TYPE, …)`, but `AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource` never sets the resource type on the per-entity resources it creates (see AdminPermissionsSchema.java around line 121), so `findByType("Groups", …)` returns only the synthetic all-groups resource created during `init()`. In addition the lambda calls `hasPermission(groupResource.getId(), …)` (a UUID produced by the resource store) while `hasPermission` resolves resources by `findByName` against the group UUID, and then `granted.add(groupResource.getId())` adds the resource UUID into a set that callers (UsersResource.searchForUser and BruteForceUsersResource.searchForUser) treat as group IDs to populate `UserModel.GROUPS`. The net effect is that group-specific VIEW_MEMBERS/MANAGE_MEMBERS permissions are completely ignored; only a permission on the all-groups resource can populate the set. As a consequence, an admin whose only permissions are scoped to a specific group will not be filtered to members of that group when listing users, and the new test `testCanViewUserByViewGroupMembers` cannot pass under FGAP V2.

findings.title: Individually-created resources are not tagged with their resource type
findings.body: In `getOrCreateResource` the path that creates a missing per-entity resource (`resource = resourceStore.create(resourceServer, name, resourceServer.getClientId()); … resource.updateScopes(…)`) never calls `resource.setType(resourceType)`. By contrast `init()` does set the type when it pre-creates the all-groups/all-users/all-clients resources. Anything that relies on `ResourceStore.findByType` (such as GroupPermissionsV2.getGroupIdsWithViewPermission, which iterates `findByType("Groups", …)`) will therefore only see the synthesised resources and miss the per-entity ones. Add `resource.setType(resourceType);` after `updateScopes` so that later type-filtered lookups see per-entity resources.
